⚠️ **IMPORTANT: alias with a missing/unresolvable target silently degrades to the direct entry — the exact silent-resolution failure mode AC5 bans**

`resolve_entry` falls through to the model's own direct entry when the alias target has no row in the merged table (`bench/fa_usage.py:443-471`, fallthrough at line 467):

```python
if isinstance(target, str) and target:
    entry = price_entry(table, target)
    if entry is not None:
        return entry, target
entry = price_entry(table, model)   # ← silent fallback
```

Concrete failure: an operator dispatches with
`FA_BENCH_PRICING='{"usd_per_mtok":{},"aliases":{"kimi-for-coding":"kimi-k2-7-code"}}'`
(dash instead of dot — the official id is `kimi-k2.7-code`). The target resolves to no entry, the code silently prices `kimi-for-coding` at its own `$0` plan entry, and the summary renders a plain `0.0000` real-billing cell — no `*` label, no "estimate @ … rates" line, no warning. The operator believes they configured a labelled K2.7-Code-rate estimate and instead gets a silent misconfiguration, which is precisely the "resolution must be loud" contract this PR establishes (AC5).

Suggested fix: validate the alias map once in `load_pricing_resolved` (after base + override merge, where `warnings` is in scope): for every `alias → target` pair, warn loudly when `price_entry(table, target)` is `None` (e.g. `⚠️ pricing: alias "kimi-for-coding" → "kimi-k2-7-code" has no entry in the loaded table — alias ignored`). Alternatively return a warning from `resolve_entry` and surface it in `render`. A regression test (alias → missing target ⇒ warning present + no unlabelled cost) would pin it.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION (new this round): a shapeless override still flips the `Pricing` source row to "override active" while contributing nothing**

`bench/fa_usage.py:426`:

```python
otable, oaliases = _pricing_parts(odoc, what, warnings)
for model, entry in otable.items():
    ...
aliases.update(oaliases)
source = f"{what} over repo default {default}"   # ← set even when the doc was rejected
```

Verified this run: an override that parses as JSON but has no `usd_per_mtok` table (`{"rates": {}}`, or just `{}`) emits the loud warning (`env override FA_BENCH_PRICING (file …): no usd_per_mtok table — ignored`) — but the code then still sets `source` to `env override FA_BENCH_PRICING … over repo default …`, and the effective table is exactly the repo default. The summary's `| Pricing |` row therefore claims an active override on a run that priced entirely at the repo default.

The load-failed path right above (lines 413–415) gets this right — it appends `"(⚠️ FA_BENCH_PRICING override failed — see pricing warnings)"` to the source instead. A doc rejected by `_pricing_parts` contributed nothing and should take the same route (or at least the same source suffix), so the Pricing row can never overstate what the run used. The loudness contract is met by the warning; this only aligns the source label with reality.
